evidence_quotes.quote: Por tanto, el objetivo de este artículo es realizar un recuento y análisis de los casos de injusticia ambiental que derivaron en recomendaciones emitidas por la CEDHJ entre enero del 2000 y agosto de 2022
Para identificar estas recomendaciones se realizó una búsqueda en el archivo digital de la CEDHJ de los casos que tuvieran por concepto la violación al derecho al ambiente sano.

La temática de la contaminación del agua mayormente recae en la categoría justicia distributiva debido a que no existe una distribución justa del recurso hídrico de calidad, es decir, el agua contaminada llega a las comunidades más vulnerables.

Para esta sección se eligieron los casos de injusticia ambiental en torno a la cuenca hidrológica Lerma-Chapala-Santiago, el caso del mal manejo de residuos sólidos en el sitio de disposición final Los Laureles, y el caso de contaminación de suelo del municipio Autlán.

en la falta de una regulación efectiva para las corporaciones de los corredores industriales que provocan daños a la salud a partir de la contaminación de los cuerpos de agua; y en el manejo de residuos en los vertederos que operan bajo concesiones que permiten una disposición final deficiente, la cual se suma a la contaminación del agua y del suelo en Jalisco.

criterion_notes.c1: Fails Criterion 1. The paper examines environmental injustice and violations of the human right to a healthy environment (derecho al medioambiente sano) in Jalisco, Mexico, across environmental degradation themes (water body contamination, biodiversity loss, municipal solid waste landfills, noise, soil agrochemical pollution, and air pollution). Although one sentence on PDF Page 9 notes in passing that 13 recommendations in the 'Contaminación del agua' category relate to water contamination, lack of supply, and privatization, the study conducts no analysis of household or community water or sanitation service access; its water analysis addresses industrial pollution of surface water bodies (Río Santiago and Lago Chapala) and chronic health effects.
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain broad wording of Criterion 2 (plain=yes) because it examines institutional human rights oversight (recommendations issued by the Jalisco State Human Rights Commission, CEDHJ) and state/municipal environmental regulatory omissions regarding industrial pollution, landfill concessions under NOM-083, land-use permits, and agrochemical enforcement. However, it fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2 (narrow=no) because it does not examine any rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community water or sanitation service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, tenure/documentation rules, tariffs, service enforcement, or utility regulatory structure). Note that even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the study is still excluded (plain_criterion2_decision='exclude') because it fails Criterion 1 and Criterion 4.
criterion_notes.c3: Passes Criterion 3. Contains qualitative empirical documentary analysis coding 35 recommendations issued by the CEDHJ between January 2000 and August 2022 into an analytical database, supplemented by documentary case studies of three environmental pollution cases.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4. Reports counts and environmental-justice classifications (distributive, procedural, recognition) of 35 CEDHJ recommendations on violations of the right to a healthy environment, alongside environmental pollution and public health impacts (e.g., renal disease/mortality near Río Santiago, landfill leachate/fires at Los Laureles, and herbicides in schoolchildren's urine in Autlán). Reports no outcome measuring water or sanitation service access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or service exclusion.
criterion_notes.c5: Fails Criterion 5 with respect to review scope. While the documentary unit of analysis (35 CEDHJ recommendations on environmental human rights violations in Jalisco) and qualitative case-study design are identifiable, no household or community water or sanitation service-access exposure or access outcome is identified or measured.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish (with English abstract). Per Criterion 10, Spanish full text is directly readable and feasible to translate/assess without language barriers, though the paper is substantively ineligible on topic/scope grounds.

study_design: Qualitative documentary content analysis and multiple case study of state human rights commission recommendations
population_and_sample: 35 recommendations on violations of the right to a healthy environment issued by the Jalisco State Human Rights Commission (CEDHJ) between January 2000 and August 2022 in Jalisco, Mexico (unit of analysis: institutional human rights recommendation), plus three environmental pollution case studies (Lerma-Chapala-Santiago basin, Los Laureles landfill, and Autlán de Navarro)
exposure: Environmental degradation/pollution and regulatory omissions addressed in CEDHJ human rights recommendations (industrial surface-water contamination, land-use change/biodiversity loss, municipal solid waste landfill management, and agricultural pesticide contamination)
outcome: Number and typology (distributive, procedural, and recognition environmental justice) of CEDHJ recommendations for violations of the right to a healthy environment (2000-2022) and qualitative environmental health impacts in three pollution cases
rationale: Exclude under E01 (Wrong topic). This qualitative documentary study analyzes 35 recommendations issued by the Jalisco State Human Rights Commission (CEDHJ) from 2000 to 2022 concerning violations of the constitutional right to a healthy environment (derecho al ambiente sano) across environmental injustice themes (surface-water pollution, biodiversity loss, solid waste landfills, soil pesticide contamination, noise, and air pollution), detailing three cases of industrial river pollution, landfill mismanagement, and agrochemical exposure. It does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access (c1=no), does not analyze a rule-type mechanism governing water or sanitation service access under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification (c2=no, though it passes the plain governance wording of c2), and reports no water or sanitation service access outcomes (c4=no).
